name: Firefly Trail (spatial span)
one_liner: Fireflies (tiles) light up one-by-one in a growing sequence and the child taps them back in the same order, or in reverse.
interaction: N tiles in a 3x3 grid flash sequentially; the child reproduces the sequence by tapping tiles, and a Backward toggle asks for reverse order. Re-tapping a selected tile de-selects it (logged as a revision). The trial auto-submits at N taps; span rises by 1 after a correct trial and drops by 1 after an error (Levitt 1-up/1-down staircase).
self_teach: A wordless ghost-hand watches three tiles flash then taps them in order and shows a check mark (about 6s), followed by one unscored warm-up trial; no text is required.

learning_science.why: A standardized, language-free index of visuospatial short-term memory that dissociates from verbal span.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use a 3x3 tile grid with sequential lighting and same-order tap-back as the core mechanic.
learning_science.source: Kessels, R. P. C., van Zandvoort, M. J. E., Postma, A., Kappelle, L. J., & de Haan, E. H. F. (2000). The Corsi Block-Tapping Task: standardization and normative data. Applied Neuropsychology, 7(4), 252-258.

learning_science.principle: Capacity limit of about four chunks
learning_science.why: Working-memory capacity centers near 3-5 items, so a staircase around this range maximizes information at the tail.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Start span at 3 and adapt by plus/minus 1; extend the item bank to spans 8-9 for above-level probing.
learning_science.source: Cowan, N. (2001). The magical number 4 in short-term memory: A reconsideration of mental storage capacity. Behavioral and Brain Sciences, 24(1), 87-114.

learning_science.why: Backward reproduction adds central-executive manipulation beyond passive storage.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Offer a Backward mode and report the forward-minus-backward manipulation cost.
learning_science.source: Baddeley, A. D., & Hitch, G. (1974). Working memory. In G. H. Bower (Ed.), The Psychology of Learning and Motivation (Vol. 8, pp. 47-89). Academic Press.

new_measurements_proposed.name: Memory span threshold
new_measurements_proposed.usefulness_tail: The staircase-estimated longest sequence a child reliably reproduces is a continuous, fine-grained capacity index that keeps separating high performers who all hit ceiling on fixed-length items.
new_measurements_proposed.how_to_collect: Track the highest sequence length reproduced correctly under a 1-up/1-down span staircase; average the last several reversal lengths.
new_measurements_proposed.how_much_to_collect: 6-10 adaptive trials per mode (forward/backward) for a stable threshold.

new_measurements_proposed.name: Manipulation cost
new_measurements_proposed.usefulness_tail: The drop from forward (storage) span to backward/reorder (manipulation) span isolates central-executive manipulation, which tracks fluid reasoning better than raw storage at the tail.
new_measurements_proposed.how_to_collect: Compute forward max span minus backward or sorted max span under matched staircases.
new_measurements_proposed.how_much_to_collect: Enough trials in each mode to estimate both spans (6-10 each).

tail_precision_rationale: Reproduction accuracy is dichotomous and saturates fast among gifted children, so this type extracts tail signal from process: the staircase-estimated span threshold (M-SPAN) and max reached (M-DIFFREACH) give a continuous capacity index above grade level, forward-minus-backward manipulation cost (M-MANIPCOST) isolates executive manipulation from passive storage, and consistency measures (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) plus order-vs-item error typing (M-ERRTYPE) separate secure high-capacity solvers from lucky ones by scoring on lapses rather than raw speed.
age_rationale: Wordless, tap-only and language-free, so it runs from K-1 (framed as catching fireflies, spans 2-3) upward; older bands unlock the Backward mode and spans of 6-9. Targets are large (66px) to remove fine-motor demands for little hands; only tapping (no drag) is required.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 short forward spans (2-3) with animal framing up to 6-8 backward spans of 8-9 and denser grids
adaptive.difficulty_levers: sequence length, forward vs backward, presentation rate, grid size, optional delayed spatial-recognition array variant
adaptive.notes: Span is a native psychophysical staircase and sequences are procedurally generated, so unlimited matched clones exist for M-CONSIST parallel forms.

engagement_hook: A glowing firefly trail that visibly grows each time you succeed, so leveling up feels like lighting a longer and longer path.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Motor: tap accuracy on small or close tiles (mitigated by large targets, tap-not-drag). Familiarity: Simon-style novelty (mitigated by ghost-hand plus warm-up). Attention/ADHD: sustained attention and impulsivity can depress span and inflate variability, mimicking low capacity; flag by gating on M-ENGAGE/M-DRIFT and treating occasional lapses as process signal rather than capacity, requiring consistency across trials before a tail decision. Device: touch vs mouse latency and screen size affect tile spacing.

name: Critter Line-Up (list sorting / digit span)
one_liner: Critters (or numbers) parade by one at a time, then the child lines them up in a required order - same, reversed, or sorted by size - by tapping them into slots.
interaction: A sequence of N items is shown one-by-one on a belt; the child then fills N ordered slots by tapping items from a shuffled tray. A rule toggle sets the target order to repeat, reverse, or sort (by real-life size for animals, ascending for numbers). Tapping a filled slot returns the item to the tray (revision). It auto-submits when all slots are filled; list length adapts plus/minus 1.
self_teach: The ghost-hand watches three animals then taps them smallest-to-biggest into the slots with a check mark (about 6s); one unscored warm-up follows. Size is depicted concretely (ant to whale) so sorting needs no reading.

learning_science.principle: List Sorting working memory (storage plus manipulation)
learning_science.why: Requiring items to be reordered by a dimension taps the central executive, not just storage, and is validated in the NIH Toolbox child battery.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use a name-then-reorder-by-size mechanic with animals for young children and numbers for older ones.
learning_science.source: Tulsky, D. S., Carlozzi, N., Chiaravalloti, N. D., et al. (2014). NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery: List Sorting Working Memory subtest. Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society, 20(6), 599-610.

learning_science.principle: Phonological loop and central executive (Baddeley model)
learning_science.why: Forward span indexes the phonological/storage buffer while reorder and reverse tap central-executive manipulation.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Provide repeat, reverse and sort rules and report the manipulation cost across them.
learning_science.source: Baddeley, A. (2000). The episodic buffer: a new component of working memory? Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 4(11), 417-423.

learning_science.why: Higher-ability children impose structure (grouping, rehearsal) that shows up in serial-position and error patterns.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Score partial credit by position and log intrusion vs novel errors to reveal strategy.
learning_science.source: Miller, G. A. (1956). The magical number seven, plus or minus two: some limits on our capacity for processing information. Psychological Review, 63(2), 81-97.

tail_precision_rationale: Sorting/reversing converts a storage task into a storage-plus-manipulation task whose forward-minus-manipulation span gap (M-MANIPCOST) tracks central-executive load and fluid reasoning better than storage alone; partial-credit position scoring (M-POLY) squeezes graded tail information from each item, while intrusion vs novel error typing (M-ERRTYPE) and first-move latency (M-RTFIRST) distinguish planful reorderers from trial-and-error solvers at the cut.
age_rationale: The animal size-sort shell is meaningful and reading-free at K-1 (short lists of 2-3), while numeric ascending-sort and reverse-order shells suit 2-3 through 6-8 with lengths to 8-9. Tapping into slots (no precise dragging) keeps motor demands low; number shells assume basic numeral recognition, so young bands default to the animal shell.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 animal size-sort with short lists up to 6-8 numeric reverse/sort with long lists and mixed content
adaptive.difficulty_levers: list length, transformation (repeat/reverse/sort), content (animals/numbers), presentation rate, set similarity
adaptive.notes: Items and orders are generated; matched parallel lists support M-CONSIST and repeated adaptive testing.

engagement_hook: A critter parade you get to organize; each correct line-up makes the parade longer, like recruiting a bigger crew.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Reading/numeracy: numeric shells need numeral knowledge (young bands use animals). Motor: tap-to-place avoids drag-precision issues. Familiarity: novel reorder mechanic (mitigated by ghost-hand plus warm-up). Attention/ADHD: distractibility can inflate order errors; require cross-trial consistency (M-CONSIST) and monitor M-DRIFT before tail inferences. Cultural: animal-size knowledge is near-universal but exemplars should be verified as familiar.

name: Match Parade (n-back / dual n-back)
one_liner: A never-ending parade of characters (or grid positions plus letters) streams by and the child taps MATCH whenever the current item repeats the one from n steps back.
interaction: Stimuli appear one at a time at a fixed pace; the child taps a MATCH button (single stream) or WHERE/WHAT buttons (dual n-back: position plus letter) when the current item equals the n-back item. Responses do not advance the stream. n adapts across blocks by accuracy/sensitivity (rises at >=80%, falls at <55%).
self_teach: A wordless 1-back ghost-hand demo shows two identical animals in a row and the hand tapping MATCH with a check (about 6s), then an unscored 1-back warm-up; the continuous format becomes obvious before any scored block.

learning_science.principle: N-back as a continuous updating measure
learning_science.why: The n-back requires constant encoding, monitoring and replacement of WM contents and correlates with fluid reasoning.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use a continuous stream with a single MATCH judgment and an adaptive n level.
learning_science.source: Kirchner, W. K. (1958). Age differences in short-term retention of rapidly changing information. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 55(4), 352-358.

learning_science.why: N-back performance relates to complex-span and Gf but is not interchangeable, so it should be one of several WM types.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Report d-prime and combine with span-based types rather than treating n-back as a sole WM index.
learning_science.source: Jaeggi, S. M., Buschkuehl, M., Perrig, W. J., & Meier, B. (2010). The concurrent validity of the N-back task as a working memory measure. Memory, 18(4), 394-412.

learning_science.why: Hits and false alarms confound ability with response bias unless modeled with sensitivity.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Score with d-prime (sensitivity) and flag lure false alarms, not raw hit counts.
learning_science.source: Green, D. M., & Swets, J. A. (1966). Signal Detection Theory and Psychophysics. Wiley.

new_measurements_proposed.name: Signal-detection sensitivity (d-prime)
new_measurements_proposed.usefulness_tail: Separates true match-detection sensitivity from response bias in continuous tasks, so a cautious child and a guesser are not scored alike near the cut.
new_measurements_proposed.how_to_collect: From hits and false alarms compute d-prime = z(hit rate) minus z(false-alarm rate) with standard edge corrections.
new_measurements_proposed.how_much_to_collect: >=20 target and >=20 non-target trials for a stable estimate.

new_measurements_proposed.name: Updating cost
new_measurements_proposed.usefulness_tail: The accuracy or RT decrement per additional to-be-updated item or level indexes the efficiency of gating and replacing WM contents, a purer executive signal than static span.
new_measurements_proposed.how_to_collect: Regress accuracy (or RT) on memory load / update count and take the slope.
new_measurements_proposed.how_much_to_collect: >=4 load levels with several trials each.

new_measurements_proposed.name: Post-error adjustment
new_measurements_proposed.usefulness_tail: Slowing and accuracy recovery after an error index performance monitoring; adaptive post-error slowing (not rigid or absent) marks metacognitive control at the tail.
new_measurements_proposed.how_to_collect: Mean RT on trials immediately after an error minus mean RT after correct trials; also track post-error accuracy.
new_measurements_proposed.how_much_to_collect: >=10 error trials with valid following trials.

tail_precision_rationale: N-back is a continuous updating task rich in exactly the process telemetry CogAT omits: signal-detection sensitivity d-prime (M-DPRIME) separates true match detection from response bias, the highest sustained n (M-DIFFREACH) probes capacity above grade level, lure (n plus/minus 1) false alarms (M-ERRTYPE) reveal fragile temporal binding, and RT variability/lapses (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) with the accuracy-by-load slope (M-UPDATECOST) index worst-performance and updating efficiency rather than rewarding fast impulsive taps.
age_rationale: Continuous updating with response withholding is too demanding for most K-1 children and confounds heavily with sustained attention, so the honest floor is 2-3 (1-back), moving to 2-back at 4-5 and 2-3-back plus dual n-back at 6-8. Only a single large button (or two) is tapped, keeping motor load minimal.

adaptive.content_range: 2-3 single 1-back with pictures up to 6-8 2/3-back and dual (spatial plus verbal) n-back
adaptive.difficulty_levers: n level, single vs dual stream, presentation pace/ISI, target rate, lure density, stimulus set size
adaptive.notes: Streams are generated with controlled target and lure rates and n is a native staircase, giving unlimited matched blocks.

engagement_hook: A monster parade that keeps marching and speeds up as you level up n, so it feels like keeping a beat in a rhythm game.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Attention/ADHD is the dominant confound: n-back loads on sustained attention and impulse control, so inattentive or impulsive children can look low-capacity; separate by reporting d-prime (bias-free), tracking M-DRIFT/M-ENGAGE across the stream, weighting consistency (M-RTVAR) over speed, and gating scores on engaged blocks. Motor: a fixed pace may clip slow motor responses (mitigated by a generous response window). Familiarity: game-novelty (mitigated by warm-up). Device: audio is not required (dual uses visual letters).

name: Last Ones In (running memory / updating)
one_liner: Items stream and stop unpredictably (report the last few), or the child keeps live tallies or the latest item per category - all requiring the WM buffer to be continuously overwritten.
interaction: Three shells via toggle: (1) running span - a stream of unknown length stops and the child taps the last k items in order; (2) keep-count - the child watches and enters running counts of target symbols at the end; (3) keep-track - the child reports the most recent exemplar seen in each category. Load (k or number of bins) adapts with success.
self_teach: The ghost-hand watches a short stream then taps the last two items in order with a check (about 6s); an unscored warm-up follows. The unpredictable stop self-teaches the need to always hold the recent tail.

learning_science.principle: Memory updating and the central executive
learning_science.why: Discarding old contents and inserting new ones is a distinct executive function (updating) separable from inhibition and shifting.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use unpredictable stop points and running counters so old contents must be actively replaced.
learning_science.source: Miyake, A., Friedman, N. P., Emerson, M. J., Witzki, A. H., Howerter, A., & Wager, T. D. (2000). The unity and diversity of executive functions and their contributions to complex frontal lobe tasks. Cognitive Psychology, 41(1), 49-100.

learning_science.why: Not knowing when the list ends forces continuous rehearsal of only the most recent items, isolating updating from simple span.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Stop streams at random lengths and require report of the last k items.
learning_science.source: Pollack, I., Johnson, L. B., & Knaff, P. R. (1959). Running memory span. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 57(3), 137-146.

learning_science.why: Maintaining the latest exemplar per category requires selective, category-bound updating.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Include a keep-track shell reporting the most recent item per bin.
learning_science.source: Yntema, D. B. (1963). Keeping track of several things at once. Human Factors, 5(1), 7-17.

tail_precision_rationale: Because the endpoint is unpredictable and old contents must be discarded, this type measures updating rather than static span: the accuracy-by-load slope (M-UPDATECOST) is a direct executive index, recency accuracy on the final item and intrusion-vs-novel error typing (M-ERRTYPE) expose proactive-interference control, and partial-credit scoring (M-POLY) yields graded tail resolution where dichotomous recall would ceiling.
age_rationale: Reporting the last 2 is feasible at 2-3, but multi-category keep-track and multiple simultaneous counters demand more executive control, so those unlock at 4-5 and 6-8. Continuous updating with withholding is too taxing for most K-1 children, so K-1 is excluded and the floor is 2-3 with the simplest last-2 shell. Interaction is tap-only.

adaptive.content_range: 2-3 report-last-2 up to 6-8 last-4, three simultaneous counters, and multi-bin keep-track with numeric updating
adaptive.difficulty_levers: k (items to report), number of counters/bins, stream length and rate, distractor similarity, numeric-update steps
adaptive.notes: Streams and stop points are generated and load is a native staircase supporting matched parallel forms.

engagement_hook: A surprise freeze-frame: the parade stops when you least expect it and dares you to name the last few, like a memory snapshot challenge.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Attention/ADHD: sustained attention strongly gates updating; flag by tracking M-DRIFT/M-ENGAGE and requiring consistency before tail calls. Reading/numeracy: counter shells need counting (young bands use last-k pictures). Motor: tap-only. Familiarity: novel stop-and-report mechanic (mitigated by ghost-hand plus warm-up).

name: Catch & Freeze (go/no-go & stop-signal)
one_liner: The child taps fast to catch frequent go targets but must freeze (withhold) on rare no-go targets, or halt an already-started tap when a stop signal flashes.
interaction: Go stimuli (butterflies) require a fast tap on the play area; no-go stimuli (bees) require withholding. In stop-signal mode a go stimulus turns red after a variable delay and the child must cancel the tap; the stop-signal delay tracks up after successful stops and down after failures (staircase) to estimate SSRT. Fixed inter-trial interval; real RTs are recorded.
self_teach: The ghost-hand taps quickly on two butterflies (check marks) then visibly pulls back and freezes on a bee (about 7s); an unscored warm-up block follows. Catch-vs-freeze reads instantly with no text.

learning_science.why: A high go-rate builds an automatic response that must be actively suppressed on no-go trials, isolating inhibition.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use a high go-probability with rare no-go trials and score commission errors.
learning_science.source: Donders, F. C. (1969). On the speed of mental processes (W. G. Koster, Trans.). Acta Psychologica, 30, 412-431. (Original work 1868).

learning_science.why: The latency of the covert stop process can be estimated from a staircased stop-signal delay and indexes response control.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Add a stop-signal mode with a delay staircase and compute SSRT.
learning_science.source: Logan, G. D., & Cowan, W. B. (1984). On the ability to inhibit thought and action: A theory of an act of control. Psychological Review, 91(3), 295-327.

learning_science.why: A child's slowest and most error-prone responses predict ability better than their fastest, so consistency should be scored.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Emphasize RT variability, lapses and commission rate over mean speed.
learning_science.source: Larson, G. E., & Alderton, D. L. (1990). Reaction time variability and intelligence: A worst performance analysis. Intelligence, 14(3), 309-325.

new_measurements_proposed.name: Commission-error rate
new_measurements_proposed.usefulness_tail: Failures to withhold on no-go/stop trials index prepotent-response inhibition; low commission rates at high go-probability distinguish strong inhibitory control from impulsivity in a way speed cannot.
new_measurements_proposed.how_to_collect: Proportion of no-go/stop trials on which a response was executed.

new_measurements_proposed.name: Stop-signal reaction time
new_measurements_proposed.usefulness_tail: The estimated latency of the covert inhibitory process is one of the least coachable executive metrics; shorter SSRT marks stronger response control at the tail.
new_measurements_proposed.how_to_collect: Track stop-signal delay with a staircase and estimate SSRT (median go RT minus mean stop-signal delay).
new_measurements_proposed.how_much_to_collect: >=30 go and >=15 stop trials for a usable estimate.

tail_precision_rationale: The high go-rate builds a prepotent response so the diagnostic signal is inhibition, not speed: commission-error rate (M-COMM) indexes response-inhibition failures, the staircased stop-signal reaction time (M-SSRT) estimates the latency of the covert stopping process (one of the least coachable executive metrics), and RT variability/lapses (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) with post-error slowing (M-POSTERR) capture worst-performance and error monitoring; scoring uses M-SPEEDACC so fast-but-impulsive responding is penalized rather than rewarded.
age_rationale: Catch/freeze is embodied and language-free, so it runs from K-1 (framed as catching butterflies and freezing like a statue) through 6-8; the stop-signal (cancel an initiated action) is harder and best emphasized at 4-5 and 6-8. Only large-area tapping is needed, minimizing motor demands, and the no-go rate is a tunable difficulty lever.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 simple go/no-go with a high go-rate up to 6-8 stop-signal with staircased SSD and faster pacing
adaptive.difficulty_levers: no-go/stop probability, presentation pace, stop-signal delay (staircase), go-stimulus discriminability
adaptive.notes: Trial sequences are generated and SSD is a native staircase yielding SSRT and matched parallel blocks.

engagement_hook: A catch-the-butterfly reflex game where freezing on a bee (or a red flash) in time earns a satisfying statue moment: fast hands, quick brakes.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Attention/ADHD is the central confound: commission errors and RT variability are elevated by inattention/impulsivity and are themselves ADHD markers, so low scores must not be read as low ability; report the full process profile, gate on M-ENGAGE/M-DRIFT, and interpret these as executive-control indices alongside other WM types. Motor: device tap latency inflates RT and can mimic failed stops (mitigated by using RT distributions and variability, not absolute speed). Familiarity: mitigated by warm-up.

name: Fish School (flanker interference control)
one_liner: The child reports which way the middle fish is swimming while ignoring flanking fish that point the same or the opposite way.
interaction: Five fish appear; the child taps a LEFT or RIGHT button for the center fish's direction. Flankers are congruent, incongruent or neutral. A response deadline (with a shrinking timer bar) tightens when the child is both fast and accurate (leveling up). RT and accuracy are logged per congruency condition and missed deadlines count against.
self_teach: The ghost-hand shows an incongruent trial (center right, flankers left) and taps the RIGHT button with a check (about 6s); an unscored warm-up follows. Only-the-middle-fish reads instantly from the highlight and demo.

learning_science.why: Flanking distractors that conflict with the target create measurable interference that indexes selective attention/inhibition.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Surround a highlighted central target with congruent/incongruent flankers and measure the RT cost.
learning_science.source: Eriksen, B. A., & Eriksen, C. W. (1974). Effects of noise letters upon the identification of a target letter in a nonsearch task. Perception & Psychophysics, 16(1), 143-149.

learning_science.principle: Child attention networks (ANT) with a fish flanker
learning_science.why: A child-friendly fish flanker validly measures executive attention across development.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use fish stimuli and large directional buttons suitable from early childhood.
learning_science.source: Rueda, M. R., Fan, J., McCandliss, B. D., et al. (2004). Development of attentional networks in childhood. Neuropsychologia, 42(8), 1029-1040.

learning_science.why: Adaptive slowing after errors reflects monitoring and control, adding process signal beyond accuracy.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Track RT on trials following errors vs correct trials.
learning_science.source: Rabbitt, P. M. A. (1966). Errors and error correction in choice-response tasks. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 71(2), 264-272.

new_measurements_proposed.name: Congruency/interference effect
new_measurements_proposed.usefulness_tail: Incongruent-minus-congruent RT (flanker/Stroop) isolates interference control independent of baseline speed; a small effect at high accuracy is a strong, hard-to-game tail marker.
new_measurements_proposed.how_to_collect: Median RT on incongruent trials minus median RT on congruent trials (correct trials only).

tail_precision_rationale: Baseline choice-RT ceilings among gifted children, so the tail signal is interference control: the congruency effect (M-CONGEFF = incongruent minus congruent RT) isolates selective attention/inhibition independent of raw speed, RT variability and lapses (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) capture worst-performance, and post-error slowing (M-POSTERR) indexes monitoring; all are read through M-SPEEDACC so a small congruency cost at high accuracy, not fast guessing, defines the top.
age_rationale: Directional judgment with a big two-choice response is accessible from K-1 (fish framing, generous deadline) through 6-8, where the deadline tightens. Large arrow buttons and a single tap keep motor demands low; the center target is enlarged and highlighted so young children can locate it without instructions.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 slow-deadline directional flanker up to 6-8 tight-deadline with a higher incongruent proportion
adaptive.difficulty_levers: response deadline (staircase), proportion incongruent, flanker-target spacing, number of flankers, stimulus duration
adaptive.notes: Trials are generated with a controlled congruency mix and the deadline is a native staircase; the congruency effect needs enough trials per condition.

engagement_hook: An underwater quick-reactions game where you follow the leader fish and tune out the school; the timer bar makes staying accurate-under-speed feel like a combo.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Attention/ADHD: interference effects and RT variability rise with inattention; interpret the congruency cost alongside consistency and gate on M-ENGAGE. Motor/device: tap latency inflates RT (use within-child condition differences, which cancel baseline motor time). Vision: relies on directional discrimination - center highlighting mitigates and size should be adequate. Familiarity: mitigated by warm-up.

name: Opposite World (Stroop / day-night)
one_liner: The child must give the non-obvious answer - tap night for a sun, name the ink color not the word, or pick the numerically (not physically) bigger digit - suppressing a prepotent response.
interaction: Three shells via toggle: day/night (tap the opposite of the picture), ink color (tap the swatch matching the ink, ignoring the printed color word), and bigger-number (tap the numerically larger of two differently sized digits). Two to four response buttons; RT and accuracy are logged by congruency and capture (prepotent) errors are flagged.
self_teach: The ghost-hand sees a sun and taps the night button with a check (about 6s), teaching do-the-opposite wordlessly; an unscored warm-up follows before scoring.

learning_science.why: An automatic reading/semantic response conflicts with the required response, so suppressing it indexes inhibition.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use color-word and numerical-size conflicts where the automatic answer is wrong.
learning_science.source: Stroop, J. R. (1935). Studies of interference in serial verbal reactions. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 18(6), 643-662.

learning_science.why: A reading-free Stroop (say night to a sun) validly measures inhibition in 3.5-7 year-olds.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Anchor the K-1 band with the picture-based day/night shell.
learning_science.source: Gerstadt, C. L., Hong, Y. J., & Diamond, A. (1994). The relationship between cognition and action: performance of children 3.5-7 years old on a Stroop-like day-night test. Cognition, 53(2), 129-153.

learning_science.why: Physical size interferes with numerical-magnitude judgments, giving a language-light inhibition measure.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Add a bigger-number shell where physical and numerical size conflict.
learning_science.source: Henik, A., & Tzelgov, J. (1982). Is three greater than five: The relation between physical and semantic size in comparison tasks. Memory & Cognition, 10(4), 389-395.

tail_precision_rationale: The Stroop conflict makes inhibition, not speed, the separator: the interference effect (M-CONGEFF = incongruent minus congruent RT) and the count of capture errors (prepotent responses, tagged via M-ERRTYPE) are purer inhibition indices than overall RT, while RT variability/lapses (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) and post-error slowing (M-POSTERR) add worst-performance and monitoring signal; scoring emphasizes a low capture rate at maintained accuracy over fast responding.
age_rationale: The day/night shell is the classic preschool Stroop and works from K-1 (pictures, do-the-opposite) with no reading; ink-color needs color-word reading (4-5 and up) and numeric Stroop needs magnitude comparison (4-5 and up). K-1 therefore uses day/night only, 2-3 adds simple opposite-arrow variants, and 4-5 and 6-8 add the reading/number shells.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 day/night and opposites up to 6-8 color-word and numerical Stroop with color-word switching
adaptive.difficulty_levers: proportion incongruent, response deadline, number of response options, addition of a switching cue (name-ink vs read-word)
adaptive.notes: Stimuli are generated with controlled congruency and the switching variant adds a set-shift lever; the effect needs enough trials per condition.

engagement_hook: An Opposite-World game where doing the obvious thing is a trap, so beating your brain's autopilot is the fun.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Reading: the ink-color shell requires reading color words, so it is age-gated and not used pre-reading. Color vision: color shells can disadvantage color-blind children - use highly distinct hues and treat day/night and number shells as color-free alternates. Attention/ADHD: inhibition load overlaps ADHD; interpret capture rate with consistency and M-ENGAGE gating. Familiarity/motor: mitigated by warm-up and large buttons.

name: Rule Swap (DCCS / task-switch / rule discovery)
one_liner: The child sorts cards into boxes by a rule that can switch (color then shape), be cued trial-by-trial, or must be discovered from feedback and then silently changes.
interaction: A card is sorted into one of two boxes by the current rule. DCCS mode sorts by color for several trials then switches to shape; cued mode shows a per-card badge/border indicating the rule (rapid switching); discovery mode hides the rule (the child infers it from correct/incorrect feedback) and changes it after a run of successes. RT, accuracy, switch vs repeat, and perseverative errors are logged.
self_teach: The ghost-hand sorts a blue star into the blue box under a COLOR badge with a check (about 6s); an unscored warm-up follows. The rule badge (paint = color, shape icon = shape) makes the current rule explicit without text.

learning_science.why: Sorting by one dimension then switching to another is the canonical preschool test of cognitive flexibility.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Implement bivalent cards and a color-to-shape switch as the K-1 anchor.
learning_science.source: Zelazo, P. D. (2006). The Dimensional Change Card Sort (DCCS): a method of assessing executive function in children. Nature Protocols, 1(1), 297-301.

learning_science.why: Reconfiguring the active task set on switch trials incurs a measurable RT cost that indexes shifting efficiency.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Add a cued mixed-switch mode and compute switch minus repeat RT.
learning_science.source: Rogers, R. D., & Monsell, S. (1995). Costs of a predictable switch between simple cognitive tasks. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 124(2), 207-231.

learning_science.why: Inferring an unstated rule from feedback and shifting when it changes reveals perseverative errors linked to executive control.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Add a discovery mode with silent intra/extra-dimensional shifts and count perseverative errors.
learning_science.source: Grant, D. A., & Berg, E. A. (1948). A behavioral analysis of degree of reinforcement and ease of shifting to new responses in a Weigl-type card-sorting problem. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 38(4), 404-411.

new_measurements_proposed.name: Task-switch cost
new_measurements_proposed.usefulness_tail: Switch-trial minus repeat-trial RT/accuracy indexes set-shifting efficiency; low switch cost with maintained accuracy is a clean flexibility signal that fixed-format tests miss.
new_measurements_proposed.how_to_collect: Compare RT/accuracy on rule-switch trials vs rule-repeat trials in a mixed block.

new_measurements_proposed.name: Perseverative-error rate
new_measurements_proposed.usefulness_tail: Continuing to apply the old rule after a switch or silent rule change directly indexes failure to update task set; near-zero perseveration at high difficulty is a sharp executive marker.
new_measurements_proposed.how_to_collect: Count post-switch errors whose response matches the previously correct rule.
new_measurements_proposed.how_much_to_collect: >=6 post-switch trials per switch across several switches.

tail_precision_rationale: Set-shifting is the flexibility component of executive function that fixed-format tests cannot see: switch cost (M-SWITCHCOST = switch minus repeat RT) indexes reconfiguration efficiency, perseverative-error rate (M-PERSEV) directly measures failure to drop an outdated rule, and in discovery mode the move path (M-PATH) with trials-to-criterion captures hypothesis testing; low switch cost and near-zero perseveration at speed is a sharp, hard-to-coach tail marker.
age_rationale: The standard DCCS color-to-shape switch is calibrated for ages 3-5, so it anchors K-1; cued rapid switching and rule discovery (WCST-like) demand more control and abstract, reading-free reasoning, so they emphasize 2-3 through 6-8. Bivalent cards use color plus shape (no reading) and a single tap to a large box.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 DCCS single switch up to 6-8 cued mixed switching and discover-the-rule with silent intra/extra-dimensional shifts
adaptive.difficulty_levers: switch frequency, cue availability (explicit badge vs hidden), number of relevant dimensions, feedback delay, mixing ratio
adaptive.notes: Cards and rule schedules are generated; mixed-block switching and discovery provide native difficulty scaling and matched clones.

engagement_hook: A rule-swap sorting game where the rug gets pulled, so spotting the switch fast (or sleuthing the secret rule) is the challenge.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Attention/ADHD/EF overlap: perseveration and switch cost are affected by attention; interpret with consistency and M-ENGAGE. Working-memory load: children must hold the current rule (young children may fail from holding, not shifting) - the explicit badge in DCCS/cued modes offloads this so shifting is isolated. Color vision: the color rule uses distinct hues plus shape redundancy. Familiarity/motor: mitigated by warm-up and large targets.

name: Solve & Stash (complex span)
one_liner: The child alternates a quick judgment (is this equation right? is this pattern symmetric?) with memorizing an item, then recalls the items in order after several cycles.
interaction: Each cycle shows a processing item answered with true/false, then briefly displays a to-be-remembered item (a letter, or a highlighted grid cell). After N cycles the child recalls the items in order via a keypad or grid. Set size adapts up when recall is perfect and processing stayed accurate, down otherwise; processing is time-limited.
self_teach: The ghost-hand answers two mini-equations (true, then false) each followed by a letter, then taps the two letters back in order with a check (about 8s); an unscored warm-up follows before scoring.

learning_science.why: Complex span (interleaving processing and storage) predicts fluid intelligence because it taxes attention control, not just storage.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Interleave a distractor-processing task with storage and score the recalled span.
learning_science.source: Engle, R. W. (2002). Working memory capacity as executive attention. Current Directions in Psychological Science, 11(1), 19-23.

learning_science.why: Standardized automated complex-span tasks (operation, symmetry) are reliable individual-difference measures of WM capacity.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use operation-span (math verify plus letters) and symmetry-span (symmetry judge plus locations) shells.
learning_science.source: Unsworth, N., Heitz, R. P., Schrock, J. C., & Engle, R. W. (2005). An automated version of the operation span task. Behavior Research Methods, 37(3), 498-505.

learning_science.why: Storage span is only valid if the child actually performs the processing task rather than trading it off.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Enforce an >=80% processing-accuracy gate before crediting a storage span.
learning_science.source: Conway, A. R. A., Kane, M. J., Bunting, M. F., Hambrick, D. Z., Wilhelm, O., & Engle, R. W. (2005). Working memory span tasks: A methodological review and user's guide. Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, 12(5), 769-786.

new_measurements_proposed.name: Processing-task accuracy (complex-span gate)
new_measurements_proposed.usefulness_tail: Accuracy on the interleaved processing task gates the validity of the storage score; it detects children who trade away processing to boost recall, protecting tail comparability.
new_measurements_proposed.how_to_collect: Proportion correct on the interleaved processing judgments; enforce a minimum (e.g. >=80%) for a valid storage estimate.
new_measurements_proposed.how_much_to_collect: All processing trials in a complex-span session (typically >=15).

tail_precision_rationale: Complex span is among the strongest single predictors of fluid reasoning because it taxes attention control, not just storage: the adaptive storage span (M-SPAN, M-DIFFREACH) gives a continuous above-grade capacity index, partial-credit and position scoring (M-POLY) extract graded tail signal, and processing accuracy (M-PROCACC) gates the score - blocking children who inflate recall by neglecting the processing task, which preserves comparability of tail decisions.
age_rationale: Complex span requires simultaneous processing and storage and, for math/reading shells, academic skills, so the honest floor is 2-3 using the nonverbal symmetry shell with set size 2; operation and reading shells and larger sets suit 4-5 and 6-8. K-1 is excluded because dual-tasking with a secondary judgment overloads young executive control. Responses are taps only.

adaptive.content_range: 2-3 symmetry span (set size 2) up to 6-8 operation/reading/rotation span with set sizes 4-5
adaptive.difficulty_levers: set size, processing difficulty and time limit, processing-storage similarity, shell (symmetry/operation/counting/rotation/reading)
adaptive.notes: Processing items and memoranda are generated and set size is a native staircase; the processing-accuracy gate must be enforced for a valid span.

engagement_hook: A solve-and-stash challenge: juggle a mini-puzzle and a memory stash at once, then prove you kept both, which feels like true multitasking mastery.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Academic skill: operation/reading shells confound with math/reading ability - use the nonverbal symmetry shell for young or low-literacy children and report processing accuracy separately. Attention/ADHD: dual-tasking amplifies attention effects; gate on M-PROCACC and M-ENGAGE. Speed-accuracy trade-off on the processing task is explicitly detected by M-PROCACC. Motor/familiarity: mitigated by a large keypad and warm-up.

name: Treasure Boxes (self-ordered spatial search)
one_liner: The child hunts for gems hidden one at a time across scattered boxes and must remember which boxes already gave a gem so as never to reopen them.
interaction: Tapping a box opens it; a gem is found in exactly one box per search. Once a box yields a gem it is exhausted, so returning to it later is a between-search error, and reopening an already-empty box within the current search is a within-search (revision) error. A new gem is hidden after each find until every box has produced one; box count grows when play is clean.
self_teach: The ghost-hand opens one empty box, then the gem box, collects the gem, and does not reopen it (about 6s); an unscored warm-up hunt follows. The exhausted-box rule self-teaches through the collect animation and demo.

learning_science.principle: Self-ordered search of spatial working memory
learning_science.why: Searching without revisiting requires holding and updating a self-generated record of visited locations, a frontal-executive function.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Require finding one hidden token per search across boxes without returning to exhausted ones.
learning_science.source: Petrides, M., & Milner, B. (1982). Deficits on subject-ordered tasks after frontal- and temporal-lobe lesions in man. Neuropsychologia, 20(3), 249-262.

learning_science.principle: CANTAB Spatial Working Memory errors and strategy
learning_science.why: Between- and within-search errors and a strategy score are established, sensitive indices of spatial WM and planning.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Separate between- vs within-search errors and score search strategy (distinct start boxes).
learning_science.source: Owen, A. M., Downes, J. J., Sahakian, B. J., Polkey, C. E., & Robbins, T. W. (1990). Planning and spatial working memory following frontal lobe lesions in man. Neuropsychologia, 28(10), 1021-1034.

learning_science.why: A systematic search sequence reflects planful strategy that separates strong reasoners beyond error counts.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Log the full move path and reward few distinct starting boxes / high efficiency vs optimal.
learning_science.source: Robbins, T. W., James, M., Owen, A. M., et al. (1994). Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery (CANTAB): a factor analytic study. Dementia, 5(5), 266-281.

new_measurements_proposed.name: Between-search errors
new_measurements_proposed.usefulness_tail: Returning to a location that already yielded a token indexes failure to maintain and update a spatial WM record across searches; few between-errors at large set sizes is a strong tail separator.
new_measurements_proposed.how_to_collect: Count revisits to boxes that have already produced a token in a self-ordered search.

new_measurements_proposed.name: Search strategy score
new_measurements_proposed.usefulness_tail: The degree to which searches follow a fixed, systematic sequence (few distinct starting boxes) reveals planful strategy use that predicts giftedness beyond error counts.
new_measurements_proposed.how_to_collect: Count distinct boxes used to begin each new search (lower = more strategic); log the full move path.
new_measurements_proposed.how_much_to_collect: Higher set sizes (>=6 boxes) across several rounds.

tail_precision_rationale: This self-ordered search demands maintaining and continuously updating a spatial record of visited locations, exposing process signal a static span misses: between-search errors (M-BETWEENERR) index failure to hold where gems were already found, the search-strategy score (M-SEARCHSTRAT: few distinct starting boxes plus a systematic path via M-PATH) reveals planful strategy predictive of giftedness, and efficiency vs optimal (M-EFF) with exploration counts (M-EXPLORE) separate strategic tail solvers from flailing - all scaling with set size for above-grade resolution.
age_rationale: Finding hidden treasure and not reopening a box is intuitive and embodied from K-1 (3-4 boxes) and scales to 6-8 (up to 8 boxes). Boxes are large, well-spaced and tap-only, minimizing motor and eliminating reading demands; the growing grid provides above-level difficulty for older children.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 3-4 boxes up to 6-8 up to 8 scattered boxes with tighter spacing
adaptive.difficulty_levers: number of boxes, spatial spacing/similarity of locations, presence of a delay, token-hiding constraints
adaptive.notes: Box layouts and token locations are generated and set size is a native staircase yielding matched parallel boards.

engagement_hook: A treasure hunt where remembering where you have already dug is the whole game; filling the gem tray while playing clean feels like mastering a map.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Attention/ADHD: impulsive tapping raises within- and between-errors; distinguish impulsivity from spatial-memory failure by separating error types and gating on M-ENGAGE. Motor/device: mis-taps on close boxes (mitigated by large, well-spaced targets). Strategy familiarity: a systematic-search strategy can be partly learned, so report strategy and errors separately and use the warm-up to equalize task understanding. WM vs planning: the strategy score partly reflects planning, interpreted alongside pure error counts.

name: Order Up! (running-memory serving / order updating)
one_liner: Food items scroll along a moving belt and the child serves the LAST few in the current order into a customer's tray, binding each item to its slot as the queue keeps updating.
interaction: A belt streams food tiles one at a time at a fixed rate and the child cannot see when a customer will 'check out'. When the checkout bell rings the child fills the customer's k ordered serving slots by tapping tiles from a pantry tray, reproducing the LAST k items in order; re-tapping a filled slot returns the tile (revision). In keep-track mode the child serves the most-recent item requested for each of several customers/categories; in tally mode the child reports running topping counts. Output is produced throughout the stream (continuous serving), not only at the end; k / number of customers rises after a clean serve and falls after an error (span staircase).
self_teach: A wordless ghost-hand watches three foods roll past, the bell rings, and the hand taps the last two into the tray slots in order with a check mark (about 7s); one unscored warm-up serve follows. The bell plus slots make 'serve the most recent ones' obvious with no text.

learning_science.why: Because the checkout point is unpredictable, only the most recent items can be relied on, forcing continuous rehearsal and replacement of a rolling buffer rather than encoding a fixed list.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Stream items of unknown length and require the last k in order at an unsignalled checkout.
learning_science.source: Pollack, I., Johnson, L. B., & Knaff, P. R. (1959). Running memory span. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 57(3), 137-146.

learning_science.why: Serving each item into a specific customer slot requires binding content to position/owner, a relational-integration demand that dissociates from raw storage.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Bind served items to ordered customer slots and score order/binding errors separately from item errors.
learning_science.source: Oberauer, K. (2009). Design for a working memory. Psychology of Learning and Motivation, 51, 45-100.

learning_science.why: Keeping the last k current while new items arrive taxes the narrow focus of attention that updates its contents, predicting fluid reasoning better than passive span.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Add keep-track and running-tally shells so old contents must be actively overwritten while serving continues.
learning_science.source: Oberauer, K. (2002). Access to information in working memory: exploring the focus of attention. Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition, 28(3), 411-421.

tail_precision_rationale: Serving from a moving queue turns running span into a continuous, gradeable task: the staircase-estimated serving span (M-SPAN) and highest k reached (M-DIFFREACH) give a fine-grained above-grade capacity index that fixed-length recall ceilings on, position/partial-credit scoring (M-POLY) squeezes graded signal from every serve, the accuracy-by-load slope (M-UPDATECOST) indexes updating efficiency, and order/binding-vs-item error typing (M-ERRTYPE) with cross-form consistency (M-CONSIST) separates secure high-capacity servers from lucky ones - scoring rewards consistent correct serving, never raw speed (first-move latency M-RTFIRST is logged as process, not credited).
age_rationale: Continuous updating with an unpredictable stop is too taxing for most K-1 children (consistent with the running-updating floor), so the honest floor is 2-3 with serve-the-last-1-or-2; keep-track across several customers and running tallies unlock at 4-5 and 6-8 with longer k. Interaction is large-target tap-and-place (no drag) and the food/customer framing is language-free; numeric tally shells assume counting and are reserved for 4-5 and up.

adaptive.content_range: 2-3 serve-the-last-2 with one customer up to 6-8 last-4 across multiple customers with running tallies and faster belts
adaptive.difficulty_levers: k (items to serve), number of customers/categories, belt speed and length, distractor similarity of foods, tally target count
adaptive.notes: Belts, orders and checkout points are procedurally generated and k is a native span staircase, giving unlimited matched parallel forms for M-CONSIST and above-grade probing.

engagement_hook: A fast-food rush where you plate the freshest orders before they scroll away; each clean serve makes the line longer, like leveling up a busy kitchen.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Attention/ADHD: sustained attention gates updating, so inattentive children can look low-capacity - gate on M-ENGAGE/M-DRIFT and require cross-trial consistency before any tail call. Numeracy: tally shells need counting (age-gated to 4-5+). Motor: tap-to-place avoids drag-precision demands; large tiles. Familiarity: novel serving mechanic mitigated by ghost-hand plus warm-up. Cultural: food exemplars should be verified as familiar and non-region-specific.

name: Gatekeeper (probed running span / continuous updating)
one_liner: Creatures parade through a gate one at a time and, at unpredictable checkpoints, a guard asks the child to tap back the last few that just passed - then the parade resumes and is probed again.
interaction: A single continuous stream of creatures crosses the gate at a fixed rate. At random moments the gate closes and a checkpoint panel appears; the child taps the last k creatures in order from a palette, the panel clears, and the SAME stream resumes toward the next checkpoint. A stream contains several probes, so the child must keep a rolling window live throughout (not a single terminal recall). A numeric shell streams digits with occasional operations and probes the current running value; a keep-track shell probes the most recent creature of each colour/family. k adapts up after a clean checkpoint and down after an error.
self_teach: A ghost-hand watches three creatures pass, the gate closes, and the hand taps the last two in order with a check (about 7s); one unscored warm-up probe follows. The repeated close-and-ask makes 'always hold the most recent ones' self-teaching.

learning_science.principle: Running memory span with unpredictable probes
learning_science.why: Not knowing when (or how often) recall will be required forces continuous updating of only the most recent items, isolating updating from list memorisation.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Probe the last k at multiple random points within one ongoing stream rather than once at the end.
learning_science.source: Pollack, I., Johnson, L. B., & Knaff, P. R. (1959). Running memory span. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 57(3), 137-146.

learning_science.principle: Memory updating as a distinct executive function
learning_science.why: Repeatedly discarding superseded contents and inserting new ones is a separable updating component of executive function.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use repeated mid-stream probes and a numeric-update shell so contents must be continually overwritten.
learning_science.source: Miyake, A., Friedman, N. P., Emerson, M. J., Witzki, A. H., Howerter, A., & Wager, T. D. (2000). The unity and diversity of executive functions and their contributions to complex frontal lobe tasks. Cognitive Psychology, 41(1), 49-100.

learning_science.principle: Recency and the rolling focus of attention
learning_science.why: Accuracy across serial positions within the rolling window reveals how many recent items sit in the immediately accessible focus.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Score a recency gradient across probes and vary k to map the accessible window.
learning_science.source: Oberauer, K. (2002). Access to information in working memory: exploring the focus of attention. Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition, 28(3), 411-421.

tail_precision_rationale: Repeated within-stream probing yields signal a single terminal recall cannot: the accuracy-by-k slope across many probes (M-UPDATECOST) is a direct updating-efficiency index, partial-credit position scoring (M-POLY) builds a recency gradient that localises the accessible window, intrusion-vs-novel error typing (M-ERRTYPE) exposes proactive-interference control, and response-time variability and lapses across probes (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) capture worst-performance consistency; drift and engagement (M-DRIFT, M-ENGAGE) gate the many-probe stream so tail decisions rest on engaged, consistent updating rather than speed.
age_rationale: Holding and re-reporting the last 2 across surprise probes is feasible at 2-3; multi-family keep-track and numeric running-value updating demand more control and are reserved for 4-5 and 6-8. Continuous updating with withholding across many probes overloads most K-1 children, so the floor is 2-3 with the last-2 creature shell. Interaction is tap-only from a fixed palette; the numeric shell assumes simple addition and is age-gated.

adaptive.content_range: 2-3 last-2 creatures with sparse probes up to 6-8 last-4 with dense probes, numeric running-value updates and multi-family keep-track
adaptive.difficulty_levers: k, probe frequency and unpredictability, stream rate, numeric-update step size, number of families, palette similarity
adaptive.notes: Streams, probe schedules and numeric operations are generated and k is a native staircase; many probes per stream yield stable within-stream slopes and matched parallel forms.

engagement_hook: A guard-the-gate game of surprise checkpoints: you never know when the gate will slam shut and quiz you, so staying ready and nailing each spot-check feels like beating a memory ambush.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Attention/ADHD: surprise probes load sustained attention and impulse control, so scores must be read with consistency and M-ENGAGE/M-DRIFT gating, not as raw capacity. Numeracy: the numeric shell needs addition (age-gated). Motor: single taps from a fixed palette, no drag. Familiarity: the close-and-ask rhythm is novel but self-teaches via the ghost-hand and warm-up. Startle: the gate-close should be gentle (no loud or sudden effects) to avoid penalising sensitive children.

name: Sky Traffic Control (cued task-switching)
one_liner: A balloon that carries both a colour and a number of dots drifts down, and a per-trial signpost tells the child which rule to use - sort by colour or by number - to send it left or right.
interaction: Each trial shows one bivalent balloon (a colour AND a dot count) and a cue banner (a paint icon = use colour, a number icon = use number). The child taps LEFT or RIGHT to route the balloon: under the colour rule warm colours go left and cool go right; under the number rule odd goes left and even goes right. The cue is chosen per trial so trials are switch (cue changed) or repeat (cue same), interleaved in mixed blocks, while single-rule pure blocks provide a baseline for mixing cost. An intra/extra-dimensional variant occasionally swaps which colour set or number rule maps to which side. RT, accuracy, cue-encoding latency and switch-vs-repeat are logged, and a response deadline tightens only when the child is both accurate and controlled.
self_teach: A wordless ghost-hand shows a paint-cue trial (a red balloon routed LEFT with a check), then a number-cue trial (a two-dot balloon routed RIGHT with a check) - about 8s - followed by one unscored warm-up. The icon-to-rule mapping reads instantly with no text.

learning_science.why: Switching the active rule on a cue incurs a reconfiguration RT cost that indexes set-shifting efficiency separately from base speed.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Present an explicit per-trial cue and compute switch-minus-repeat RT in mixed blocks.
learning_science.source: Meiran, N. (1996). Reconfiguration of processing mode prior to task performance. Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition, 22(6), 1423-1442.

learning_science.why: Performing two rules in one block (even on repeat trials) is costlier than a pure block, indexing sustained task-set maintenance beyond the transient switch.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Contrast mixed-block repeat trials with pure single-rule blocks to isolate mixing cost.
learning_science.source: Kiesel, A., Steinhauser, M., Wendt, M., Falkenstein, M., Jost, K., Philipp, A. M., & Koch, I. (2010). Control and interference in task switching - a review. Psychological Bulletin, 136(5), 849-874.

learning_science.why: Cue-driven switching improves across childhood and is a sensitive, age-graded marker of executive flexibility.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Scale cue transparency, switch rate and deadline with age and report the switch cost as the key index.
learning_science.source: Crone, E. A., Bunge, S. A., van der Molen, M. W., & Ridderinkhof, K. R. (2006). Switching between tasks and responses: a developmental study. Developmental Science, 9(3), 278-287.

tail_precision_rationale: Base routing RT ceilings among gifted children, so the tail signal is flexibility, not speed: switch cost (M-SWITCHCOST = switch-minus-repeat RT/accuracy) indexes reconfiguration efficiency, cue-encoding latency (M-RTFIRST, first action after cue onset) isolates how fast the rule is loaded, and error typing (M-ERRTYPE) separates rule-confusion from mapping slips; all are read through the speed-accuracy operating point (M-SPEEDACC) and an accuracy-gated combo (M-COMBO) so only controlled, accurate routing counts, while post-error slowing (M-POSTERR) captures monitoring - a low switch cost held at high accuracy is the hard-to-coach separator.
age_rationale: Trial-by-trial cued switching with a bivalent stimulus is developmentally appropriate from 2-3 (few switches, transparent icons, generous deadline) and scales to fast mixed switching with intra/extra-dimensional swaps at 6-8. The single DCCS-style switch anchors K-1 elsewhere, so this cued-switching type floors at 2-3; the number rule assumes odd/even and dot-count skills reserved for 4-5 and up (younger bands use two colour families as both rules). Response is a single large LEFT/RIGHT tap.

adaptive.content_range: 2-3 rare well-cued colour-vs-colour switches up to 6-8 fast mixed colour/number switching with intra/extra-dimensional swaps and tight deadlines
adaptive.difficulty_levers: switch rate, cue-to-stimulus interval, deadline (staircase), rule set (colour/number), intra vs extra-dimensional swaps, congruency of the two rules on a stimulus
adaptive.notes: Bivalent stimuli and cue schedules are generated with controlled switch rates and congruency, and the deadline is a native staircase; switch and mixing costs need enough switch/repeat and pure/mixed trials per condition.

engagement_hook: An air-traffic game where the rule for steering keeps changing on the signpost, so catching each rule-swap and routing under the gun feels like a fast decision arcade.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Attention/ADHD: switch cost and variability rise with inattention - interpret alongside consistency and gate on M-ENGAGE. Colour vision: the colour rule uses highly distinct warm/cool hues with a redundant cue and offers a number-rule alternate. Reading/numeracy: the number rule is age-gated and icons carry the rule so no reading is needed. Motor/device: tap latency inflates absolute RT, so within-child switch-minus-repeat differences (which cancel base motor time) are the primary index. Familiarity mitigated by warm-up.

name: Brain Arcade Relay (integrated EF: switch + hold + stop)
one_liner: A single game rotates between three arcade stations - route-by-rule, hold-the-last-few, and go/no-go - and the child must reconfigure to whichever station's mini-game is showing.
interaction: A station banner (a wordless icon) sets the current mini-game for a short run of trials, then rotates to a different station: SWITCH (route a cued stimulus left/right), HOLD (a few items stream, then tap back the last k), and STOP (tap frequent go targets, withhold on rare no-go). The diagnostic novelty is the between-station change: the trial right after a station rotation is a global switch that requires loading a whole new task set. Per-station accuracy, the global (between-station) switch cost, commission errors on STOP, and a composite executive profile are logged; the station schedule and per-station difficulty adapt with performance.
self_teach: A wordless ghost-hand plays one trial at each station - routes a cued item, taps back the last two, taps a go target and freezes on a no-go - each with a check (about 12s), then one unscored warm-up rotation. Each station's icon and demo make its rule obvious without text.

learning_science.principle: Unity and diversity of executive functions
learning_science.why: Shifting, updating and inhibition are correlated yet separable, so a battery sampling all three yields a richer, more reliable EF profile than any single task.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Rotate switch, updating and inhibition stations and report a composite plus component scores.
learning_science.source: Miyake, A., Friedman, N. P., Emerson, M. J., Witzki, A. H., Howerter, A., & Wager, T. D. (2000). The unity and diversity of executive functions and their contributions to complex frontal lobe tasks. Cognitive Psychology, 41(1), 49-100.

learning_science.why: Reconfiguring to an entirely different task (between-station) taxes higher-order control beyond within-task rule switches, adding a distinct global-control signal.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Isolate the trial after each station rotation and score the global reconfiguration cost separately.
learning_science.source: Kiesel, A., Steinhauser, M., Wendt, M., Falkenstein, M., Jost, K., Philipp, A. M., & Koch, I. (2010). Control and interference in task switching - a review. Psychological Bulletin, 136(5), 849-874.

learning_science.why: Mobile adaptive batteries that interleave several EF tasks are engaging and give sensitive individual-difference measurement across development.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Deliver stations as adaptive arcade mini-games with a shared telemetry model.
learning_science.source: Diamond, A. (2013). Executive functions. Annual Review of Psychology, 64, 135-168.

tail_precision_rationale: An integrated relay measures control that single-paradigm tasks miss: the between-station global switch cost (M-SWITCHCOST) indexes higher-order reconfiguration, commission errors on the STOP station (M-COMM) index inhibition, and cross-station consistency (M-CONSIST) with RT variability (M-RTVAR) forms a composite executive profile scored on stable, controlled performance (M-SPEEDACC) rather than speed; whole-session drift and engagement (M-DRIFT, M-ENGAGE) gate the composite so a tail decision rests on sustained, engaged control across domains - a coherent high profile with low global switch cost is a strong, hard-to-coach separator.
age_rationale: Reconfiguring to an entirely different mini-game every rotation is a demanding global-control load, so the honest floor is 4-5 (slow rotations, two stations) rising to fast three-station rotations at 6-8; younger children are better served by the single-paradigm WM types. All stations use large-target taps and language-free icons, and the composite is only reported when each component has enough engaged trials.

adaptive.content_range: 4-5 slow two-station rotations (hold + stop) up to 6-8 fast three-station rotations with harder per-station levels
adaptive.difficulty_levers: rotation frequency, number of stations in play, per-station difficulty (k, switch rate, no-go probability, pace), cue transparency
adaptive.notes: Station schedules and per-station items are generated; the global switch cost needs enough post-rotation trials, and each component score requires a minimum engaged-trial count before the composite is formed.

engagement_hook: A brain-arcade relay where the machine keeps swapping the mini-game on you; thriving no matter which station lights up feels like proving you can do it all.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Grab-bag risk: a battery must report component AND composite scores (not a single blurred number) so distinct EF signals are preserved - handled by separate per-station telemetry. Attention/ADHD: rotating demands amplify attention effects; gate on M-ENGAGE/M-DRIFT and require per-component consistency. Working-memory load of remembering the current station is offloaded by an always-visible station banner so shifting and inhibition are isolated. Motor/familiarity mitigated by large taps and the multi-station warm-up.

name: Star Grid (simultaneous visuospatial span / change detection)
one_liner: A pattern of coloured stars flashes on a grid all at once, disappears, and after a short delay the child says whether a probed cell is the SAME or CHANGED - or taps back which cells were lit.
interaction: A set of coloured stars appears simultaneously across grid cells for a brief exposure (about 700ms) then blanks. After a short retention delay the test display returns and one cell is probed: the child taps SAME if its colour is unchanged or CHANGED if it differs (change-detection shell). A recognition shell instead asks the child to tap all the cells that had been lit (order optional). Set size (number of stars) rises after correct responses and falls after errors (staircase), and hits and false alarms feed a visual-capacity estimate. RT and accuracy are logged, but scoring is capacity/consistency-based, not speeded.
self_teach: A wordless ghost-hand watches a three-star flash, waits through the blank, sees the probe turn a different colour, and taps CHANGED with a check (about 7s); one unscored warm-up follows. The flash-then-probe rhythm teaches 'remember the picture, spot the change' with no text.

learning_science.why: Simultaneous arrays with change detection estimate the number of integrated objects held in visual WM, a capacity limited to a few items.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use brief simultaneous arrays and single-probe change detection to estimate visual capacity K.
learning_science.source: Luck, S. J., & Vogel, E. K. (1997). The capacity of visual working memory for features and conjunctions. Nature, 390(6657), 279-281.

learning_science.why: Modelling hits and false alarms yields a bias-free sensitivity/capacity index rather than confounding cautious and guessing responders.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Compute sensitivity (d-prime) and a capacity K from hit and false-alarm rates across set sizes.
learning_science.source: Cowan, N. (2001). The magical number 4 in short-term memory: a reconsideration of mental storage capacity. Behavioral and Brain Sciences, 24(1), 87-114.

learning_science.why: Change-detection capacity increases across childhood and is a sensitive, language-free individual-difference measure.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Staircase set size and report capacity to track above-grade capacity in older children.
learning_science.source: Simmering, V. R. (2012). The development of visual working memory capacity during early childhood. Journal of Experimental Child Psychology, 111(4), 695-707.

tail_precision_rationale: Simultaneous change detection extracts a continuous capacity signal that sequential span and dichotomous accuracy miss: signal-detection sensitivity (M-DPRIME) yields a bias-free visual-capacity K that separates cautious from guessing responders, the staircase set-size threshold (M-SPAN) and highest set size reached (M-DIFFREACH) give an above-grade capacity index, and change-vs-no-change error typing (M-ERRTYPE) with cross-form consistency (M-CONSIST) and lapse rate (M-LAPSE) score stable capacity rather than speed - RT is logged only as process, never credited.
age_rationale: Simultaneous change detection is a two-choice same/changed judgment that works from K-1 with small set sizes (2-3 stars) and scales to large set sizes (6-8 items) with shorter exposures and longer delays for older children. Presentation is simultaneous (no sequence to reproduce), so it complements the sequential Corsi span; targets are large well-spaced grid cells requiring only a tap.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 set size 2-3 with generous exposure up to 6-8 set sizes of 6+ with brief exposure, longer delay and a recognition-reproduction shell
adaptive.difficulty_levers: set size, exposure duration, retention delay, colour/shape similarity of items, change magnitude, single-probe vs whole-array recognition
adaptive.notes: Arrays, probes and change trials are generated with controlled change rates and set size is a native staircase; enough change and no-change trials per set size are needed for a stable d-prime and capacity K.

engagement_hook: A spot-the-difference star flash: the sky lights up for a blink and you catch whether a star changed, so holding the whole picture in your mind's eye feels like a superpower.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Colour vision: change detection uses highly distinct hues and offers a shape-change and position-recognition alternate so colour-blind children are not disadvantaged. Attention/ADHD: brief exposures load attention; gate on M-ENGAGE and require consistency before tail calls. Vision/device: exposure duration depends on display refresh, so the demo logs frame time and uses conservative exposures. Motor: single taps on large cells. Familiarity mitigated by the ghost-hand and warm-up.

name: Echo Ridge (reverse-order span)
one_liner: A sequence of stones (young) or digits (older) lights and chimes one by one, then the child taps them back in REVERSE order - the echo returns backwards - scored on span, not speed.
interaction: An arc of stones or a keypad of digits lights and chimes sequentially; after the sequence the child reproduces it in REVERSE order by tapping, with a Sort mode that instead asks for ascending order and a Forward baseline mode for manipulation cost. Re-tapping a placed item returns it to the pool (logged as a revision). The trial auto-submits at N taps; span rises by 1 after a correct trial and falls by 1 after an error (1-up/1-down staircase).
self_teach: A wordless ghost-hand watches three stones light and chime, then taps them back last-to-first with a check mark (about 7s), followed by one unscored warm-up trial; a reversed-arrow animation teaches reverse order with no text.

learning_science.why: Reproducing a sequence in reverse adds executive manipulation beyond passive storage, lifting the ceiling above forward span.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Make reverse reproduction the default and report forward-minus-backward manipulation cost.
learning_science.source: Baddeley, A. D., & Hitch, G. (1974). Working memory. In G. H. Bower (Ed.), The Psychology of Learning and Motivation (Vol. 8, pp. 47-89). Academic Press.

learning_science.why: Pairing visual lighting with an auditory chime engages the phonological loop and visuospatial sketchpad together, stabilising encoding for young children.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Light and chime each item so the sequence is encoded in two modalities before reverse recall.
learning_science.source: Baddeley, A. (1992). Working memory. Science, 255(5044), 556-559.

learning_science.why: Working-memory capacity centres near 3-5 items, so a staircase in this range maximises information at the tail.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Start span at 3 and adapt by plus or minus 1, extending to spans of 8-9 for above-level probing.
learning_science.source: Cowan, N. (2001). The magical number 4 in short-term memory: A reconsideration of mental storage capacity. Behavioral and Brain Sciences, 24(1), 87-114.

tail_precision_rationale: Reverse reproduction converts a storage task into storage-plus-manipulation: forward-minus-backward span (M-MANIPCOST) isolates central-executive manipulation, the staircase span threshold (M-SPAN) and max reached (M-DIFFREACH) give a continuous above-grade capacity index, position partial-credit (M-POLY) and order-vs-item error typing (M-ERRTYPE) plus cross-form consistency (M-CONSIST) score secure capacity rather than speed, and first-tap latency (M-RTFIRST) is logged as process only, never credited.
age_rationale: Reverse manipulation is beyond most K-1 children, so the honest floor is 2-3 with short spatial spans (matching backward Corsi at 2-3); the digit-reverse shell and longer spans suit 4-5 (matching backward digit span) and 6-8. Interaction is tap-only on large targets, and the digit shell assumes numeral recognition so younger bands default to the stone shell.

adaptive.content_range: 2-3 short spatial reverse spans up to 6-8 long digit reverse and ascending-sort spans
adaptive.difficulty_levers: span length, reverse vs ascending-sort vs forward baseline, presentation rate, spatial vs digit shell
adaptive.notes: Sequences are procedurally generated and span is a native staircase, giving unlimited matched parallel forms for M-CONSIST and above-grade probing.

engagement_hook: An echoing canyon where your taps must bounce the sequence back in reverse; the glowing trail grows longer every time you nail it.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Reading/numeracy: the digit shell needs numeral knowledge, so young bands use the stone shell. Motor: tap-not-drag with large targets. Attention/ADHD: manipulation load overlaps attention, so require cross-trial consistency (M-CONSIST) and gate on engagement before tail calls. Familiarity: the reverse mechanic self-teaches via the ghost-hand and warm-up. Auditory: chimes are an aid, not a requirement, since visual lighting alone conveys the sequence for muted devices or deaf and hard-of-hearing children.

name: Ghost Trail (reverse path retrace)
one_liner: A firefly hops across lily pads tracing a path, then the child sends it home by retracing the path in REVERSE (or forward), a spatial span with manipulation.
interaction: A ghost firefly hops from pad to pad along a path of N pads shown by a moving light; the pads reset and the child taps pads to send the firefly home by RETRACING the path in reverse (last pad back to first), with a Forward baseline mode. Re-tapping undoes the last hop (logged as a revision). The path auto-submits at N taps; length rises by 1 after a correct retrace and falls by 1 after an error (staircase).
self_teach: A wordless ghost-hand watches a three-pad trail, then taps the pads in reverse (end to start) with a check mark (about 7s); one unscored warm-up follows. A reversed footprint animation teaches retrace-backwards with no text.

learning_science.why: A standardized, language-free index of visuospatial short-term memory that dissociates from verbal span.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use sequential spatial locations reproduced by tapping as the core mechanic.
learning_science.source: Kessels, R. P. C., van Zandvoort, M. J. E., Postma, A., Kappelle, L. J., & de Haan, E. H. F. (2000). The Corsi Block-Tapping Task: standardization and normative data. Applied Neuropsychology, 7(4), 252-258.

learning_science.why: Reverse reproduction adds central-executive manipulation beyond passive storage.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Make reverse retrace the scored mode and report forward-minus-reverse cost.
learning_science.source: Baddeley, A. D., & Hitch, G. (1974). Working memory. In G. H. Bower (Ed.), The Psychology of Learning and Motivation (Vol. 8, pp. 47-89). Academic Press.

learning_science.why: Remembering a traversed path taxes the visuospatial sketchpad and is separable from static pattern span.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use a traveled path (not simultaneous dots) so sequence order is intrinsic to the route.
learning_science.source: Della Sala, S., Gray, C., Baddeley, A., Allamano, N., & Wilson, L. (1999). Pattern span: a tool for unwelding visuo-spatial memory. Neuropsychologia, 37(10), 1189-1199.

tail_precision_rationale: Retracing a traveled path in reverse taxes visuospatial manipulation: the staircase path span (M-SPAN, M-DIFFREACH) is an above-grade capacity index, forward-minus-reverse cost (M-MANIPCOST) isolates manipulation, and the logged move path (M-PATH) with efficiency versus the correct route (M-EFF) and order-vs-item error typing (M-ERRTYPE) separate planful reversers from trial-and-error solvers; scoring is capacity- and consistency-based, with first-move latency (M-RTFIRST) logged as process only.
age_rationale: Forward path retrace is intuitive and embodied from K-1 (short 2-3 pad trails), while reverse retrace (the manipulation mode used for coverage) unlocks at 2-3 and scales to long trails at 6-8. Pads are large and well-spaced, tap-only and reading-free, and the growing trail provides above-level difficulty for older children.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 short forward trails up to 6-8 long reverse retraces with denser pad fields
