construct_irrelevant_risks: Motor: two large choice cards, coarse taps. Familiarity: wordless demo plus per-rule warm-up. Reading: none; rules are pictorial. Device: untimed; only within-child switch cost and perseveration are interpreted, cancelling device latency.

name: Home Again (object-location binding)
one_liner: Watch which animal lives in which house, then after they come out and shuffle put each animal back in its own house.
interaction: During encoding, N distinct animals each appear briefly in a distinct house on a 3x3 grid, then vanish. The animals reappear in a tray; the child taps an animal then taps its remembered house (tap a filled house to send its animal back). When all are placed the bindings are scored and the set size adapts up on a fully-correct round.
self_teach: Wordless demo: two animals show in their houses, vanish, and a ghost hand taps each animal then its house (turning green); one unscored 2-animal warm-up before scoring. Pure tap-tap, no reading.

learning_science.principle: Feature/relational binding in working memory (episodic buffer)
learning_science.why: Item-to-location binding taxes the episodic buffer and relational memory, dissociable from serial-order or item-only span and closely tied to fluid reasoning.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Score WHICH animal goes WHERE (binding), not the order of visits; the error taxonomy separates swaps (mis-binding) from empty-house (lost-location) errors.
learning_science.source: Baddeley, A. (2000). The episodic buffer: a new component of working memory? Trends in Cognitive Sciences.

learning_science.why: Binding distinct identities to distinct locations is a relational-memory operation that adds tail variance beyond storage capacity.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use distinct objects (not one repeated token) so each placement is an identity-location association.
learning_science.source: Cohen, N. & Eichenbaum, H. (1993). Memory, Amnesia, and the Hippocampal System.

learning_science.principle: Adaptive span staircase; accuracy over speed
learning_science.why: Consistency of correct binding, not speed, is the ability signal (worst-performance logic).
learning_science.concrete_decision: Set size staircases 1-up/1-down above grade; first-placement latency is logged as planning and never rewarded as speed; consistency across matched set sizes is reported.
learning_science.source: Conway, A. et al. (2005). Working memory span tasks: a methodological review. Psychonomic Bulletin & Review.

tail_precision_rationale: Binding span (M-SPAN/M-DIFFREACH via an above-grade set-size staircase) keeps separating high performers who all ceiling on short lists, and the swap-vs-empty error split (M-ERRTYPE) reveals whether failures are mis-bindings (identities kept, associations scrambled) or lost locations - a finer grain than a right/wrong span. Consistency across matched set sizes (M-CONSIST) lowers the conditional error at the cut.
age_rationale: Tap-to-place with large targets and set size 2 suits K-1; the above-grade staircase (up to ~6-8 bindings) gives headroom for 6-8. No timed pressure and no fine motor beyond tapping.

adaptive.content_range: 2 up to ~8 item-location bindings on a 3x3 (extensible) grid
adaptive.difficulty_levers: set size; encoding time; grid size / spatial proximity of houses; visual similarity of animals; optional retention delay
adaptive.notes: Fully procedural: sample distinct objects and distinct cells; matched parallel forms clone trivially for consistency estimates.

engagement_hook: The animals come out to play and mix themselves up - a warm 'everyone home!' puzzle where getting them all back feels great.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Motor (tap-tap only, large targets); verbal labeling could aid rehearsal (use hard-to-name similar animals at high bands); spatial-only strategies (distinct identities force binding, not pure location memory); scale encoding time with set size so it measures binding, not exposure.

name: Acorn Keeper (delayed span across a filled retention interval)
one_liner: Remember which burrows the squirrel fills with acorns in order, shoo crows during the wait, then tap the burrows back in order.
interaction: A sequence of burrows lights with acorns (encode order). Then a filled retention interval begins: crows appear and the child taps them to shoo them for a staircased duration, blocking rehearsal. When the wait ends the child taps the burrows back in the original order. Span AND the survivable delay both staircase; shoo-accuracy gates validity.
self_teach: Wordless demo: two burrows fill, a crow appears and a ghost hand taps it, then the ghost taps the burrows back in order (green); one short unscored warm-up. Taps only, no reading.

learning_science.why: A filled retention interval isolates resistance to forgetting/interference - distinct from immediate span or per-item complex-span processing.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Insert a distractor-filled delay AFTER encoding and staircase its duration as the key lever.
learning_science.source: Peterson, L. & Peterson, M. (1959). Short-term retention of individual verbal items. Journal of Experimental Psychology.

learning_science.why: Without an attention-demanding filler, span reflects rehearsal, not maintenance; the crow task guarantees the delay is truly filled.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Require active shoo-taps during the delay and log shoo-accuracy as a processing gate.
learning_science.source: Brown, J. (1958). Some tests of the decay theory of immediate memory. Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology.

learning_science.why: Accumulating interference is diagnostic of maintenance robustness.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Reuse a small burrow set so proactive interference grows; report drift across the block.
learning_science.source: Keppel, G. & Underwood, B. (1962). Proactive inhibition in short-term retention of single items. Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior.

tail_precision_rationale: Two orthogonal staircases - set size (M-SPAN) and survivable filled-delay duration (M-DIFFREACH) - give a 2-D maintenance ceiling that keeps separating children who all hit immediate-span ceiling. The shoo-accuracy gate (M-PROCACC) protects comparability by discounting trials where the delay was not truly filled (rehearsal leak), drift (M-DRIFT) flags proactive-interference build-up, and order-vs-wrong-burrow errors (M-ERRTYPE) add process grain.
age_rationale: Short spans and brief delays with a simple tap-the-crow filler suit K-1; longer delays and larger spans extend the ceiling to 6-8. Everything is tap-based with no reading.

adaptive.content_range: span 2-6 crossed with retention delays ~2.5-9s of active distraction
adaptive.difficulty_levers: set size; retention-interval duration; distractor rate/load during the delay; burrow-set reuse (proactive interference)
adaptive.notes: Procedural sequences and delays; matched forms clone easily; the distractor can be swapped (shoo / count) without changing the span construct.

engagement_hook: Guard your acorns while pesky crows swoop in - a playful 'hold it in your head' challenge with a satisfying shoo.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Motor speed on the distractor (shoo pace is easy and only occupies attention, it is not scored for speed); reading (none); rehearsal leakage (gated by shoo-accuracy); keep the filler attention-demanding enough to block rehearsal but not so hard it becomes a second span task.
